messages.subject: M2 -- different results from mirt 1.28 and mirt 1.30
parts:
Dear Dr. Chalmers, 
I have installed mirt 1.3 on my main computer and I'm still using mirt 1.28 on an old computer.

Within the same model (attached to this message) and script, the TLI and CFI are different. 

mirt 1.3
M2(graded_uni_gm, type="C2")
            M2   df p     RMSEA   RMSEA_5  RMSEA_95      SRMSR       TLI       CFI
stats 303990.7 1127 0 0.4361045 0.4346468 0.4372552 0.08620609 0.1837313 0.2177425

mirt 1.28
M2(graded_uni_gm, type="C2")
            M2   df p     RMSEA   RMSEA_5  RMSEA_95      SRMSR       TLI       CFI
stats 19211.1 1127 0.1065652  0.1052071  0.1078534  0.08620609   0.9390815  0.9416198


Could you clarify this situation?
Any help will be appreciated.

Thank you

PS: Thanks for having this supportive forum.

As I said in the beginning, I do appreciate all your effort to keep this forum as a supportive place where we can talk directly to you and solve our questions.
thank you so much.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: M2 -- different results from mirt 1.28 and mirt 1.30
parts:
The change happened in this commit: https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/commit/aec5ab95a850040e06a172de94c6307974f00be7

The initial form used some incorrect summations, resulting in a collapsed table of derivatives that were incorrect. Overall, this resulted in some conservative estimates for C2, making models appear better than they should have, which I did not notice right away (this was detected by a few others who use mirt, and was therefore patched immediately). The results now give the anticipated behavior in terms of Type I error control and power. 

As a general rule, brand new features should be treated as alpha releases since they could potentially have bugs that I was not aware of yet. The longer something has been in the package though, the better tested it is, and therefore the more trustworthy. That principle is true of most software, so open-source is no different. Cheers.

Phil
